The local realization of generating series of finite Lie rank

lax-825748·registered·created 15 Oct 2026·GitHub @dc84fb0·Lean v4.33.0 epoch · mathlib db584cd6d46c

      Abstract

      A real noncommutative generating series admits a finite-dimensional analytic differential representation if and only if its Lie rank is finite and it satisfies the convergence condition on ordered products of Lie polynomials. The Lie rank is the least representation dimension. Two representations of that dimension are equivalent by an analytic change of coordinates fixing the origin.

      The algebraic foundation consists of shuffle multiplication, the Poincaré–Birkhoff–Witt theorem, and formal coordinates on the annihilator of a finite-codimension Lie subalgebra. The analytic argument uses factorial estimates for iterated vector fields, convergence of residual series, and the analytic inverse function theorem. Convergence is expressed by geometric bounds on commutative power-series coefficients. Both the output and all vector-field coefficients are required to converge.

      The submission includes the real-coefficient algebraic foundation and its proofs, so it has no dependencies on other archive submissions. The source paper records the three approved corrections to the analytic statements and estimates.

      The LaTeX sources of the paper were taken from the heuklyd papers collection.
